title: Godot crashes (maybe) because of animated sprite 2d and scene loading
body: ### Tested versions (v4.6.1) (Idk what a commit hash is) (I have not done testing with a separate project et cetera to check reproducibility as I am an amateur dev on a game jam deadline and it would take me too much time to try and reproduce the setup if I even can. I was told by a moderator in the forum to post here, sorry if this is poorly written) (Notably I updated from 4.1.1 to 4.6.1 because I was having a similar issue previously, and have continued to have it) ### System information Godot v4.6.1.stable - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9144) - 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i3-12100F (8 threads) - 15.81 GiB memory ### Issue description I am not a very experienced programmer and this error is mostly beyond me so I will do my best to describe what is happening FIRST I have many parts of my (3d) game using animated sprite 3d/2d. I use it for objects, enemies, and the player's left and right hands. The relevant nodes are the animated sprite 2d nodes for the player's hands as I have not had this issue when implementing this with the enemies a day prior to when implementing player hand animations. Previously I used much simpler and smaller textures for testing. Now I use 7680/4320 textures for the hands. One AnimSprite2d is on top of the other in the ui, the second (Right hand) is flipped. Most aspects of functions and the like for the player, enemies, and objects, are in scripts in "Component" Node3Ds, inside a Node3D each named "Components" as a child to the main body. This includes the player's hand animation manager node and script. Currently I have each AnimSprite2d saved as its own scene which is loaded by the player's sprite SECOND I have had this issue with two setups in different versions: 4.1.1 Simple: I used v4.1.1 and AnimSprite2ds with an animation for each item and their states (Empty Idle, Empty Punch, Water Jug Idle, Water Jug Use) 4.1.1/4.6.1 Saved Nodes: I separated the animations into separate AnimNode2ds with one animation each and saved them as scenes. Then I now instantiate what I need when it is needed. The idea was that, if the issue was the engine loading high resolution textures in animations that were not playing so that they would be cached or something, then I would force the engine to not do that by just not having them actively exist. I queue_free() the nodes and .instantiate load("path") of the AnimSprite2ds depending on the states of the hands (idle, attacking, items, etc). THIRD 4.1.1 Simple: If (3 or more high definition animations were existing in the node at once)?: My entire pc would lag, more over time, severely after starting running until the editor would crash behind the game window, then lag would disappear. 4.1.1 Saved Nodes: If 3 or more (var NAME = load("animnode2d_path") were un-commented at once: My entire pc would lag, more over time, severely after starting running until the editor would crash behind the game window, then lag would disappear. 4.6.1 Saved Nodes: If 3 or more (var NAME = load("animnode2d_path") were un-commented at once: My entire pc would lag, more over time, severely after starting running until the editor would crash behind the game window, then lag would disappear. FOURTH For some reason in the last example (4.6.1 Saved Nodes) the issue disappeared for a while (a day). I have no idea why. Now, a similar issue happens. This time I have added animations for the Referee Flag item. The game lags severely as described before (much faster than before I think) and then instead of properly crashing, an error message appears "The instruction at 0x00007FF857530711 referenced memory at 0x00000000000000160. The memory could not be read. Click on OK to terminate the program" and then the editor crashes behind the game window. The game seems to run fine after that (?) For more screenshots of this issue as I have encountered it I have linked the forum help areas where I stared into the void and lost my mind: (This one was before the issue described but maybe maybe maybe is relevant I have no idea. There are also screenshots for context of how the game looks) https://forum.godotengine.org/t/godot-const-prefab-is-completely-broken-how-do-i-fix-this-im-on-a-gamejam-time-limit/135288 https://forum.godotengine.org/t/editor-has-a-bug-solved-game-lags-until-editor-crashes-then-the-lag-disappears-and-game-window-stays-open-editor-is-crashed/135778 https://forum.godotengine.org/t/editor-crash-with-error-box-instruction-at-referenced-memory-could-not-be-read/135930 **If any more information is needed please ask** ### Steps to reproduce (I do not have the time to try and reproduce it myself atm because of aformentioned gamejam deadline and lack of experience (I constantly cross reference code as I constantly forget functions etc) and how convoluted my current project is) I **assume** it is reproducible by - Creating an animated sprite 2d/3d with large textures (4x scale 1820/1080) - (multiple animations inside the node's animation component or multiple of this node with different animations) open in the editor during runtime, or something entirely different? (when I got the window's error crash I had no nodes open except the main scene) ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) Again I dont think I myself am capable of reproducing this right now. This says it requires a rather small project too. If you need the entire game project file so far honestly you can have it since I might not even be able to make it to the jam because of this bug anyways but bleh srry. I get this is a required field I just cant fill it. (I have not done testing with a separate project et cetera to check reproducibility as I am an amateur dev on a game jam deadline and it would take me too much time to try and reproduce the setup if I even can. I was told by a moderator in the forum to post here, sorry if this is poorly written)
